name: Cerebral Diseases of Vascular Origin with Epilepsy
aliases: Epilepsy Secondary to Cerebral Vascular Disease

criteria.description: Presence of cerebral vascular lesions confirmed by neuroimaging
Clinical evidence of recurrent epileptic seizures consistent with epilepsy
Exclusion of other primary epileptic or neurodegenerative disorders
EEG abnormalities consistent with epileptiform activity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of cerebral vascular lesions and recurrent epileptic seizures with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on clinical presentation and neuroimaging findings; no universally accepted formal criteria exist.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal epileptic seizures with motor manifestations
searchTerms: motor seizures in specific brain area
loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision

rare.symptomName: Movement disorders secondary to vascular lesions
searchTerms: movement problems from brain vessel damage
abnormal movements due to vascular lesions

laboratory: Normal or nonspecific blood tests; exclusion of metabolic causes
Coagulation profile abnormalities in some cases
imaging: MRI showing cerebral infarcts, hemorrhages, or vascular malformations
CT scan demonstrating ischemic or hemorrhagic lesions
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; possible association with vascular risk factor polymorphisms
other: EEG demonstrating epileptiform discharges localized to vascular lesion areas

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of vascular lesions on neuroimaging
No history of stroke or vascular events
Progressive cognitive decline without acute vascular events

redFlags: Sudden onset of focal neurological deficits
references: Orphanet: Cerebral diseases of vascular origin with epilepsy - ORPHA:166487
